queue.title: F129+F132 spec loop round 1 ONLY - requirement drift is unreachable from both surfaces
queue.detail: ROUND 1 ONLY. Do NOT proceed past R1 on this item - see decision D5 in decisions_for_user. This is not a bug fix, it is two missing surfaces, and an unattended run should not build UI overnight without the operator seeing the proposal. FINDINGS.md F129 (driven 31/31, scripts/drive/t_row10_drift.py) and F132 (static, not driven). The engine is CORRECT: evidence footprints on the right branch and commit, a change to a footprinted file raises exactly one candidate naming that file, coverage moves to drifting and back to verified, resolution holds against a re-scan. But POST /spec/drift/detect is the ONLY writer of a RequirementDrift row - no scheduler sweep, no MCP tool, no second route - and hub/ui/src never calls it. F132 is the sequencing constraint and the reason to be careful: requirement_gate still refuses `approved` on `drifting` with the remedy 'resolve the drift candidate', an action no surface offers, and detect_drift never closes an open candidate so it cannot self-heal. The symmetry is what keeps the gate usable today, so shipping a Detect button ALONE - the obvious cheaper half - would strand tasks in approved-refused with no exit but a hand-written API call. Detect and resolve ship together, or resolve first. Write the proposal, then STOP and move to the next queue item.

decisions_for_user.question: The drive will find new defects. Which should be fixed unattended and which merely filed?
decisions_for_user.pre_authorised_default: FIX what is small, self-contained, and unambiguous - a wrong status code, a missing field on a response, a message that names the wrong thing - each with a test and its own commit.
